For the State : Mr. Naveen Kr. Gaunjhu, Advocate
For O.P No.2 : Mr. Sanjay Kumar, Advocate
 ---------
08/ 30.09.2024
Heard learned counsel for the parties.

2. Petitioner is apprehending his arrest in connection with Bhawanathpur P.S. Case No. 88 of 2022 for the offences registered under Sections 341, 323, 452, 379, 498A, 504, 34 of the IPC and Section  of Dowry Prohibition Act, pending in the court of learned Judicial Magistrate, 1st Class, Garhwa.
3.
Despite receiving notice by the mother of the informant, no one turned up on behalf of informant.
The present case pertains to matrimonial discord between the petitioner/husband and the informant/wife.
It is alleged that there is demand of Rs.4,00,000/- and one motorcycle by this petitioner.

It further appears that in District Court, mediation took place between petitioner/
husband and informant/wife, however, it was not successful at this stage.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner shall join investigation and appear before the court concerned as and when required.
5. Learned APP further opposed the prayer for anticipatory bail and submitted that there is specific allegation against this petitioner.

6. Considering the fact that the present case pertains to matrimonial discord between the parties and nothing has been brought to notice of this Court that either petitioner would flee away from the justice or temper with the evidence, if admitted to anticipatory bail, as such, I do find it a fit case to grant anticipatory bail to the petitioner.

sentences.text:
Accordingly, petitioner, above named, is directed to surrender before the learned court below within four weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order and the learned court below on his surrender, shall release him on bail on furnishing bail bonds of Rs. 10,000/- (Rupees Ten thousand)
with two sureties of the like amount each, to the satisfaction of learned Judicial Magistrate, 1st Class Garhwa, in connection with Bhawanathpur P.S. Case No. 88 of 2022, subject to the conditions as laid down under section 438(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure.
